tags.name: South Button
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-10 - CORRECTION. All three sources re-pulled this pass consistently describe SHALLOW coral reefs (Wikipedia and andamanislands.com both explicitly say reefs as shallow as 1.8m/6ft; none of the three mentions a wall or a 25m drop-off). The previously recorded 'western wall to 25 metres' and 'leopard shark' claims do NOT appear in any current source and could not be re-confirmed - removed as unsupported (likely carried over in error from an earlier pass). Depth corrected from 25m to 12m and difficulty from Intermediate to Beginner to match the shallow-reef profile sources actually describe. Confirmed marine life this pass: manta rays and devil rays (all 3 sources), snappers/sweetlips/groupers/butterflyfish/barracuda (andamanislands.com + wikipedia), turtles (all 3), dugongs (wikipedia only - noted as park-wide fauna, not asserted as a diver sighting). Remains validated=true on the corrected facts.

tags.name: Duncan's Wreck
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-10 - WRECK HISTORY UPGRADE. Found an independent maritime-history source, theshipslist.com (Inch Steamship Co. fleet list), that cross-confirms and extends the previously-uncertain tonnage claim: vessel launched 1923 by J. Priestman & Co Ltd, Sunderland, as 'Barbara Marie' (4,290 GRT - now independently confirmed, not just dive-shop sourced). Sold/renamed multiple times: Portsea (1925), Cipro (1933, Italian owners), Stella (1937); captured by HMS Circassia 14 Aug 1941 off Cape Verde, taken into Ministry of War Transport service as Empire Planet; sold 1947 to Williamson & Co, Hong Kong, renamed Inchkeith; struck an uncharted rock 2 March 1955 near Port Meadows/Duncan Island and was declared a total loss. This is a new, verifiable pre-wreck history not previously in the markdown - added since it is corroborated by a dedicated ship-history reference source, not just dive operators. Depth (6-22m), length/beam (111m x 16m), cargo (coal and timber), and route (Calcutta-Bombay) all still confirmed by frogman.in and seahawksscuba.in. Updated validation_source to add theshipslist.com.

tags.name: Dixon's
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-10. IMPORTANT: the previously-cited diveindia.com URL (2018/01/02/1st-dive-shop-in-the-andamans) now 404s, as does diveindia.com/our-story - diveindia.com appears to have restructured its site and this content is no longer live there. Replaced with scubadiving.com ('How Three Brothers Put Havelock Island Diving on the Map'), a Scuba Diving Magazine feature that independently corroborates the discovery narrative: Karen-community brothers Johnny, Jackson, and Dickson (Poayasay/Poayesay - spelling varies by source) worked for DIVEIndia founder Vandit Kalia; Dickson's Pinnacle was the first of the three put on the Havelock map in 2006, followed by Johnny's Gorge and Jackson's Bar. Depth (16-35/40m), 19km distance from Havelock, and marine life (Napoleon wrasse, manta rays, barracuda, trevally, reef sharks, turtles, yellow soft corals, barrel sponges) reconfirmed by diveandaman.com and frogman.in. Did not add 'whale sharks' - only frogman.in mentions this, not corroborated elsewhere.

tags.name: MV Primrose
tags.note: Re-audited 2026-07-10. Protected site near North Sentinel Island; diving prohibited. Added South China Morning Post as a 4th independent source, which resolves the crew-count discrepancy: SCMP confirms 31 total crew (21 of them Hong Kong nationals) and 16,000-ton Panamanian-registered cargo vessel, matching NZ Herald's 31 figure. The UPI archive headline's 'twenty-eight sailors' remains an outlier not matching the other three sources - noted as such rather than resolved. 2 August 1981 grounding date, ONGC helicopter rescue, Captain Liu Chunglong, and 1991 Mohamed Brothers salvage attempt all still confirmed by at least 2 sources. Wikipedia's North Sentinel Island article confirms Sentinelese scavenged iron from the wreck but (this pass) does not itself specify 'arrowheads' - that detail traces to the previously-cited geosat.space, which is not used as a citation here; keeping the description to what the 3-4 current sources support (iron scavenging, not the specific end-use of the metal).
